description_en: Kularatna Vihāra isa branch of Cikã Bahī. It can be accessed via a narrow alley that runs under a residential building on the way to Cyāsal from Bhelāchẽ. The west-facing god house has a carved door, but lacks atoraṇa.There are no stone lions in front of the door and even the panels of the door are not fixed in place. A stone image of Akṣobhya can be found inside the sanctum - this small image is a replacement of the previous one, which was stolen in the 1960s. To the left of Akṣobhya, one can see a stone statue of a six-armed Mañjuvajra. He holds a sword and an arrow in his two right hands and performsvaradawith the third one. His three left hands can be seen holding a book of thePrajñāpāramitā, alotus flower and a bow. Tārā sits to the right of Akṣobhya, and is performingvaradaandabhayaand holding lotus stalks in her two hands. To the left of Tārā, one can find a terracotta image of Red Matsyendranātha. His body is covered with a red cloth. According to local informants, this particular image was installed around 40 years ago.Thisvihārais attached to the eastern boundary wall of a courtyard that measures 23 m x 8 m. The courtyard can be accessed through an opening on its western wall, which also contains images of Bhīmasena and Gaṇeśa. The building is a simple one-storey structure, and its back wall shares the courtyard's boundary wall. The three other sides are partitioned with timber lattice work. The main door is to the west, and is a swing door with metal vertical rails. The building is raised above the level of the courtyard in that it sits on a stone plinth of 1.8 m x 2.4 m.It appears that the plinth was recently covered with a concrete flat slab that is supported by brick piers on the western side. The roof has astūpafinial that has been built with bricks on cement mortar. In front of the sanctum, one can find a smalldharmadhātumaṇḍala. The western residential building in front of thevihārahas some remaining traditional wall paintings on the first floor level, though these are rapidly deteriorating.No inscription could be found to provide information about the establishment of thisvihāra. However,Gellner(1987, 405) mentions that the nearby Bhaiṣajya Vihāra was established by Jīvanṛsiṃha in 1878 (NS 998). He claims that his eldest son established this Kularatna Vihāra some years later.
description_ne: भेलाछेँबाट पूर्व हुँदै च्यासलतिर लाग्दा बाटोको उत्तरपट्टिको गल्लीबाट भित्र गएपछि कुलरत्न विहारमा पुगिन्छ । यो सप्तपुर महाविहार (चिकं बही) को शाखा विहार हो । विहारभित्र पस्न कुनै ढोका बनाइएको छैन । पश्चिमाभिमुख एकतले सानो देवलको खम्बा र छत सबै आधुनिक शैलीले ढलान गरिएको छ । विहारको गर्भगृहभित्र पस्ने ढोकामा केही काष्ठकला देखिन्छ, तर ढोकामा खापा हालिएको छैन । ढोकामाथि तोरण राखिएको छैन र ढोकाको दायाँ-बायाँ सिंह पनि छैनन् । गर्भगृहभित्र अक्षोभ्यको शिलामूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । करिब ६०-७० वर्षअगाडि अक्षोभ्यको मूर्ति चोरी भएपछि नयाँ मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको हो । अक्षोभ्यको बायाँपट्टि मञ्जुवज्रको शिलामूर्ति राखिएको छ । छ हात भएका मञ्जुवज्रले दायाँ हातहरूमा खड्ग र वाण लिएका छन् अनि अर्को हात वरद मुद्रामा छ भने बायाँ हातहरूमा प्रज्ञापारमिता पुस्तक, कमलको फूल र धनुष लिएका छन् । अक्षोभ्यको दायाँपट्टि दुबै हातले कमलको डाँठ लिएकी ताराको शिलामूर्ति छ । ताराको दायाँपट्टि रातो मत्स्येन्द्रनाथको माटोको मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको छ । उनको पूरै शरीर कपडाले छोपिएको छ । स्थानीयका अनुसार करिब ४० वर्षअगाडि मात्र उक्त मूर्ति स्थापना गरिएको हो ।विहार परिसरमा एउटा धर्मधातु मण्डल राखिएको छ । यो विहारको स्थापना कहिले भयो भन्नेबारे कुनै अभिलेख पाइएको छैन । तर १८७८ (नेसं ९९८) मा यस विहारको सँगै रहेको भैषज्य विहार बनाइएको थियो र त्यसको केही वर्षपछि भैषज्य विहार बनाउने व्यक्तिकै जेठा छोराले कुलरत्न विहार बनाएका थिए (Gellner 1987, 405) ।
